name: Cord
overview: The Bible presents the cord as a practical and symbolic tool used in various ancient contexts, including fastening tents and binding individuals, as seen when Samson was bound with new cords (Judges 15:13) and in the construction of the tabernacle (Exodus 35:18; 39:40). Cords also played a role in measuring land and casting lots, reflecting God’s provision and order among His people (Joshua 17:14). Figuratively, cords represent spiritual realities such as blessings, sin, life, and friendship, while symbolically they signify mourning and inheritance, highlighting their significance beyond mere physical use (Job 36:8; 39:10).
